bib.title: Memory-R1: Enhancing Large Language Model Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning

question: Can reinforcement learning with outcome-based rewards teach LLM agents to manage an external memory bank (ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP) and to filter retrieved memories before answering?
hypothesis: RL is the missing ingredient for adaptive memory in LLM agents; outcome rewards suffice to learn memory operations and distillation.
contributions: First RL framework for memory-augmented LLMs: Memory Manager plus Answer Agent with memory distillation
Data-efficient PPO/GRPO fine-tuning with as few as 152 QA pairs
Analysis of RL choices, model size and memory design

method.summary: Two LLM agents fine-tuned separately with PPO or GRPO using exact-match answer reward: a Memory Manager choosing ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP per extracted fact (rewarded via a frozen Answer Agent's correctness) and an Answer Agent that distils 60 retrieved memories then answers. Trained on LoCoMo only; zero-shot on MSC and LongMemEval.
method.task: long-term conversational memory management and QA over multi-session dialogue

datasets.name: LoCoMo
datasets.size: about 600 turns, 26k tokens per dialogue (App B: averaging 300 turns, 9k tokens)
datasets.preprocessing: Memory Manager data: GPT-4o-mini builds temporal memory bank from preceding turns (text says 24 turns in B.2, 50 in Algorithm 1), fused with current turn and linked QA; no operation labels. Answer Agent data: 60 retrieved memories (top 30 per participant) + question + gold answer.

datasets.name: LongMemEval
datasets.split: six task types plus overall (SSU, SSP, OD, MS, KU, TR)

models.name: Memory-R1 (PPO / GRPO)
models.architecture: Memory Manager + Answer Agent, two separately tuned copies

other.use: builds temporal memory banks for training data; stronger manager in Fig 6

training.objective: PPO clipped objective (Eq 2) or GRPO with group-normalised advantage and KL to reference (Eq 3); reward = exact match of predicted vs gold answer (Eq 4). Memory Manager trained with Answer Agent frozen; Answer Agent trained with Memory Manager fixed.
training.lr: PPO actor 1e-6, critic 1e-5 (GRPO: actor only, lr not stated separately)
training.regularisation: GRPO KL term beta (value not stated); PPO clip epsilon (value not stated); GRPO group size G not stated

inference.samples: single run; no seeds or variance reported
inference.prompting: Memory Manager and answer prompts adapted from Mem0 and MemGPT (Figs 9-11); answer under 5-6 words, lists selected memories before **Answer:**
inference.retrieval: similarity-based RAG, 60 candidate memories per question (top 30 per participant)

metrics.name: LLM-as-a-Judge (J)
metrics.definition: separate LLM labels answer CORRECT or WRONG vs gold, generous grading (Fig 12)

eval.protocol: all baselines re-implemented on LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen-2.5-7B, temperature 0, max 2048 tokens; single run, no significance tests

availability.data: LoCoMo CC BY-NC 4.0; MSC and LongMemEval public

prompts.text: You are a smart memory manager which controls the memory of a system. You can perform four operations: (1) add into the memory, (2) update the memory, (3) delete from the memory, and (4) no change.

You are an intelligent memory assistant tasked with retrieving accurate information from conversation memories. ... 9. IMPORTANT: Select memories you found that are useful for answering the questions, and output it before you answer questions. 10. IMPORTANT: Output the final answer after **Answer:**
Your task is to label an answer to a question as 'CORRECT' or 'WRONG'.

limits: Dialogue-centric datasets only; multimodal extension untested (authors).
Memory Manager and Answer Agent trained separately for stability under sparse rewards; end-to-end multi-agent RL left to future work (authors).
Single runs, no seeds or confidence intervals; judge model not named; GRPO group size, KL beta, clip epsilon, steps and epochs not given; no code release stated.
Text inconsistencies: 24 vs 50 turns for temporal memory bank; 26k tokens/600 turns vs 9k/300 turns for LoCoMo; intro compares to Mem0 while Sec 4.2 compares to MemoryOS.
Gains on LongMemEval are mixed for PPO with Qwen (J 47.40 below A-Mem 54.80).
